name: tasklist
title: Understanding tasklist
summary: Displays running processes on local or remote Windows systems, with options to filter, format, and show modules, services, and verbose details.

examples.description: Lists all running processes on the local computer in a table.
Shows verbose details for processes that are not responding.
Lists only processes whose image name matches chrome.exe.
Outputs, in CSV without headers, processes using more than ~500,000 KB of memory.
Shows which services are hosted by each svchost.exe instance.
Lists processes that have loaded ntdll.dll (and shows loaded modules).
Prompts for the password and lists processes on remote host SRV01 using the specified credentials.

permissions.notes: Local use typically works as a standard user. Remote use (/S) generally requires local administrator rights on the target, proper credentials (/U, /P), network connectivity, and firewall allowance for RPC. UAC remote restrictions may block administrative local accounts unless using the built-in Administrator or appropriate policy settings.

risk.warning: tasklist is read-only, but frequent remote enumerations can add minor overhead and will create authentication and audit log entries.

output_fields.name: IMAGENAME
output_fields.description: Executable name of the process; use to identify the application (e.g., chrome.exe, svchost.exe).

output_fields.name: PID
output_fields.description: Unique process identifier; essential for correlating logs and for targeted termination with taskkill.

output_fields.name: MEMUSAGE
output_fields.description: Approximate working set in KB; high values can indicate memory leaks or runaway processes.

output_fields.name: STATUS
output_fields.description: Indicates RUNNING, NOT RESPONDING, or UNKNOWN; helps quickly spot hung apps.

output_fields.name: USERNAME
output_fields.description: Account under which the process runs; useful for security context and ownership checks.

output_fields.name: CPUTIME
output_fields.description: Cumulative CPU time used; sustained high values can indicate CPU-bound processes.

output_fields.name: SERVICES (with /svc)
output_fields.description: Lists Windows services hosted in the process; critical for mapping svchost.exe instances to services.

output_fields.name: MODULES (with /m or /m module.dll)
output_fields.description: Shows loaded DLLs; useful for dependency and injection analysis.

output_fields.name: SESSIONNAME and SESSION#
output_fields.description: Terminal Services session information; helps identify interactive vs. service sessions.

output_fields.name: WINDOWTITLE (with /v)
output_fields.description: Top-level window title for GUI apps; helps match processes to visible windows.

common_errors.message: INFO: No tasks are running which match the specified criteria.
common_errors.meaning: Your /FI filter returned no results. The criteria may be too restrictive or misspelled.
Insufficient rights to enumerate processes (common on remote systems without administrative privileges or due to UAC/remote restrictions).

common_errors.message: ERROR: The RPC server is unavailable.
common_errors.meaning: Remote enumeration failed; the target may be offline, RPC blocked by firewall, or RPC service not available.

common_errors.message: ERROR: The network path was not found.
common_errors.meaning: Bad hostname/IP or name resolution/connectivity issue when using /S to query a remote system.
A parameter or switch is misspelled or unsupported. Check TASKLIST /? for valid options.
